description: Inputs on which parseGate3Switch (src/ingest/sources/services.ts) breaks the oracle invariant, findings that this branch reports but may not fix (services.ts is out of its scope). Kinds 1-4: the oracle (tests/fixtures/gate3_oracle.py) says unknown and the hand reader gives a determinate answer; oracle must be null. Kind 5: the hand reader misses a coding cookie Python honours (U+2028 or U+2029 between '#' and 'coding' on line 1 or 2, where the '.' of encodingProblem's regex stops), so it reads the bytes as UTF-8 while Python decodes them with the declared codec; these include OPPOSITE VALUES (oracle true, hand false) and answers on modules Python rejects (oracle null). Kind 5 is listable only when the test's hiddenCookie() check passes on the input itself, so no other opposite value, answer on a rejected module or missed rebinding can be listed. Kind 6 (oracle null): the module imports itself (app.api.swap.constants) and uses the import; run under that name, Chain.ETH can be this file's own ETH = RealChain.ZCASH, so the hand reader's false is the opposite of what running it gives for the first six entries. Matched by exact src, hand verdict, oracle verdict, kind and labels. When services.ts is fixed the oracle test reports the entry as stale: delete it. Same on Python 3.9, 3.11 and 3.13.

from app.api.common.models import Chain

# Default slippage percentage for providers that do not support automatic
# slippage computation
DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_PERCENTAGE = "0.5"

# Chains temporarily excluded from swap/bridge routing entirely.
#
# Zcash is disabled because Brave Wallet currently sends a shielded-only
# unified address (u1...) as the swap recipient. Bridge providers honour
# whatever recipient they are given, so the payout lands in a shielded pool the
# wallet cannot scan: the funds arrive, but are invisible to the user.
#
# Re-enable by removing Chain.ZCASH here, once brave-core ships (and uplifts)
# the fix that sends a transparent recipient. Pair that with a
# recipient/refund_to validation guard that rejects shielded addresses, so
# shielded support doesn't come back accidentally before Ironwood ships.
SWAP_DISABLED_CHAINS: frozenset[Chain] = frozenset({Chain.ZCASH})
SWAP_DISABLED_CHAINS: "frozenset[Chain]"
